Firmware library

Keep the firmware images your appliances run — upgrade images and install media — in one checksummed library that the upgrade, boot-partition and provisioning flows pick from.

👤 ForAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsusers.manage
📍 WhereFortiWeb ADOM → Administrator → Firmware (URL /web/firmware/); also in the FortiAnalyzer ADOM's Administrator menu

What is it?#

The Firmware library stores firmware images on the SATOM node so that nobody has to upload a several-hundred-megabyte file for every device. Each image is recorded with its product, version, build, platform and a SHA-256 checksum. The appliance Upgrade and Boot Partition pages, the Upgrade Flow and Provisioning choose their images from here.

What does it do?#

  • Uploads images with a live progress bar; the SHA-256 is then computed in the background and you are notified when the image is ready.
  • Keeps two families of images apart:
  • Upgrade (.out) — applied to a running appliance.
  • Install — media to build a new machine (.out, .zip, .qcow2, .ova, .ovf, .vmdk, .img, .gz, .tgz), optionally tagged with a hypervisor (KVM or VMware ESXi).
  • Fills in Version and Build from a Fortinet filename (for example FWB_KVM-v7.6.8.M-build1128-FORTINET.out → 7.6.8, build 1128). A value you typed is never overwritten.
  • Lists, downloads and deletes images. Deleting removes the file from disk.
  • Publishes a machine-readable manifest of the library (/web/firmware/manifest.json), regenerated on every upload and delete.
  • Scopes the library to the ADOM: a product ADOM sees, downloads and deletes only its own product's images and cannot upload for another product; Global sees everything.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: download and delete follow the active ADOM like the list; an image of another product answers 404 Not Found in a product ADOM. The Upgrade and Boot Partition pages no longer offer install images.

Requirements#

  • An administrator profile.
  • The image file, at most the node's upload limit (the page states up to 600 MB).

Permissions#

Every route of the library requires users.manage (administrators).

🔑Permission — Without the permission

The Firmware menu entry is part of the Administrator menu group, which is only drawn for administrators. The URLs answer 403 Forbidden. Operators still choose images on the appliance Upgrade page; they only cannot add or remove them.

The menu entry exists in the FortiWeb and FortiAnalyzer ADOMs. The page also opens in the FortiADC ADOM by URL.

How to use#

Upload an image#

  1. Open Administrator → Firmware.
  2. Under Add a firmware image, choose the Firmware file.
  3. Pick the Image type: Upgrade (.out) or Install / new machine. For an install image, pick the Hypervisor (Any / hardware, KVM .qcow2, or VMware ESXi (.ovf / .ova)). The file picker only offers the extensions the type accepts.
  4. In Global, pick the Product. In a product ADOM the product is fixed.
  5. Check Version and Build (filled in from the filename when possible). Version is required.
  6. Check the Platform: Any (universal), Hardware appliance or Virtual Machine (KVM/VMware/cloud). Fortinet's file name carries it (FWB_KVM-…, FGT_VM64_KVM-… = VM; FWB_1000E-…, FGT_60F-… = hardware), so choosing the file fills it in and the label reads (detected from the file name). It also fills the hypervisor of an install image. A platform you pick yourself is kept; a name that does not say leaves Any.
  7. Optionally add Notes (Release notes / source / GA build).
  8. Click Upload.

A toast Uploading FWB_KVM-v7.6.8… shows the transfer. The upload keeps running while you move to other pages. Once the file is on the node, a job Verifying FWB_KVM-v7.6.8… computes the checksum, and a notification says Firmware image ready: FWB_KVM-v7.6.8.M-build1128-FORTINET.out — SHA-256 verified — 210 MB. Ready for upgrades. The Stored firmware table reloads.

Download or delete an image#

  • Download saves the stored file.
  • The delete button asks Delete firmware 7.6.8 (FWB_KVM-v7.6.8.M-build1128-FORTINET.out)? This removes the file from disk. and confirms Deleted firmware fortiweb 7.6.8 (…).

Use an image#

Images are not applied from this page. Go to the appliance and use Upgrade or Boot Partition — see Firmware upgrade — or plan a window with Upgrade Flow.

Configuration#

Field Description Required Example
Firmware file The image. Accepted extensions depend on the image type. Yes FWB_KVM-v7.6.8.M-build1128-FORTINET.out
Image type Upgrade (applied to a running appliance) or Install (builds a new machine) Yes (default Upgrade) Upgrade (.out)
Hypervisor Install images only: any/hardware, KVM or VMware ESXi No KVM
Product Product the image is for. Only offered in Global. Yes in Global FortiWeb
Version Firmware version; filled from the filename when possible Yes 7.6.8
Platform Universal, hardware or VM; detected from Fortinet's file name, also on backup-server pulls. The Upgrade page offers an image to an appliance whose platform matches (the appliance's probed hardware type, else its model), or when either side is universal/unknown. No Virtual Machine
Build Build number No 1128
Notes Free text No GA build

The Stored firmware table shows Product, Type, Version, Platform, Build, File, Size, SHA-256, Uploaded by and Uploaded (UTC).

Example#

🧪Example — Preparing a FortiWeb upgrade to 7.6.8

  1. Download the VM and hardware .out images from the vendor.
  2. Upload each with Image type Upgrade and the matching Platform.
  3. On a FortiWeb VM, Upgrade now offers only the VM and universal images, newest first, with their checksum prefix.

Result#

  • A library row with metadata and checksum; the file is stored on the node in a folder per image.
  • Audit entries firmware.upload (with the checksum, or pending while it is computed) and firmware.delete.
  • The manifest is rewritten.

Troubleshooting#

"A firmware version is required (e.g. 7.6.4)."#

Possible causes — The filename does not carry a version and the field is empty.

Solution — Type the version.

"Unsupported file type ".qcow2" for an upgrade image. Accepted: .out."#

Possible causes — The file is install media but Image type is Upgrade (or the other way round).

Solution — Pick Install / new machine for VM install media.

"Please choose a firmware .out file to upload."#

Solution — Choose a file before clicking Upload.

"Your session expired — please reload and try again." / "Invalid or missing CSRF token — reload the page and try again."#

Possible causes — The page was open for longer than the session.

Solution — Reload the page and upload again.

"Firmware upload failed" notification#

Possible causes — The checksum job could not read the file, for example because the disk is full.

Solution — Check free space on the node and upload again.

The image does not appear on an appliance's Upgrade page#

Possible causes - The image's Product differs from the appliance's kind. - The image's Platform is Hardware and the appliance is a VM (or the other way round). - The image's Type is Install. Install media builds a new machine and is not a flash payload; only Upgrade images are offered. - You uploaded in another ADOM; product ADOMs only see their own product.

Solution — Check product, type and platform in the Stored firmware table.

Advanced#

Advanced Integrity

The checksum recorded at upload is checked again every time an image is read for a flash. A file that changed on disk is refused (sha256 mismatch … recorded …, file …) before anything is sent to a device.

Advanced How the upload survives navigation

The page sends the file in a single upload request. It keeps running when you change pages because navigation in SATOM does not unload the page.

Advanced ADOM rule on upload

The ADOM of the request decides the product, not the form. A hand-crafted upload in the FortiADC ADOM is always filed as a FortiADC image.

#firmware#image#.out#upload#sha256#install image#qcow2#ova#repository#manifest
